dailyInsight.headline: Audit the first-admin path before you call an email-less setup a login flow
dailyInsight.insight: QM's fresh administrator-login source describes a deliberately narrow bootstrap handoff: an operator may create a five-minute, one-use link only for a configured administrator, and the portal checks its purpose, intended origin, current role, and replay state before it issues a session. Operators of comparable portals can audit whether their own first-admin route has those separate boundaries rather than one broad setup exception.
dailyInsight.mechanism: The CLI creates a purpose-bound HMAC token with a configured administrator subject, portal-origin audience, short expiration, and random identifier, then puts it in a URL fragment. Opening the URL only renders a confirmation page; a same-origin POST verifies the token, queries current administrator rights, consumes the identifier through a durable claim, and only then creates the ordinary portal session.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: Bootstrap is a high-pressure moment: someone needs access before ordinary identity plumbing is ready. A route that distinguishes deployment control, a pre-existing role, a short credential, human confirmation, live authorization, and one-time redemption gives the operator places to inspect and revoke instead of silently turning missing email into missing access control.

actions.audience: Operators and builders of self-hosted portals with an initial-administrator workflow
actions.label: Trace the bootstrap credential from issue to redemption
actions.instruction: In a disposable test environment, document who can mint the first-admin credential, whether it is bound to one origin and short lifetime, whether opening it avoids creating a session, whether redemption rechecks current authorization and consumes a one-time identifier, and whether an unavailable replay store fails closed. Do not use production deployment secrets or real administrator credentials.

receipts.title: feat(auth): allow operator admin login without email
receipts.supports: The merged public source adds the operator command, portal redemption route, email-less boundary, token validation, and focused tests that define the proposed bootstrap handoff.

receipts.title: QM CLI: Administrator login without email
receipts.supports: The public operator documentation states that the command selects an existing org_admin, produces a private one-use link for five minutes, and must not put that credential in shared logs.

receipts.title: QM admin-login token and redemption contract tests
receipts.supports: The public tests specify rejection for another portal, expiration, altered purpose, malformed identifiers, and a token signed for a different purpose; the accompanying integration contract covers one successful redemption and a rejected replay.

confidence.basis: Fresh public implementation, operator documentation, and token tests agree on the same bounded design, but the reporting did not execute a live deployment and the integration scenario is opt-in.

dailyInsight.limitation: These receipts establish designed source behavior, not a released or configured instance, safe handling of the printed credential, or the suitability of this route for every organization. The selected principal is still an email-shaped existing grant; ordinary users still need email or another identity path.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise this call if public source or tests show a link can create a session on GET, be redeemed cross-origin or more than once, survive a revoked administrator grant, or issue a session when current-role or replay-state checks are unavailable.
dailyInsight.watchNext: Watch whether ordinary email or external identity setup preserves the same narrow boundary rather than letting the bootstrap route quietly become a permanent alternative authentication channel.
